:::{#exm-minimum-description-length-maximum-likelihood}
#### Equal codeword lengths for the coin flips

<!-- no-figure: the example is two chosen models -->

The $9$ models of @exm-two-part-description-length have codewords of equal length,
so @thm-minimum-description-length-maximum-likelihood applies to the data of $70$ heads in $100$ flips.
The chunk below compares the model with the shortest two-part description length
to the model that gives the flips the highest probability.

```{r}
#| label: minimum-description-length-maximum-likelihood
likelihood <- success_prob^n_heads * (1 - success_prob)^(n_flips - n_heads)
success_prob[which.max(likelihood)]
success_prob[which.min(total_bits)]
```

Both models have the probability of heads $`r success_prob[which.max(likelihood)]`$,
as the theorem says.

:::
